statements.text: To prove the inequality LHS > RHS, calculate their difference LHS – RHS and show that it is positive (LHS – RHS > 0). Formula: $LHS - RHS > 0$
If a condition like a > b is given, rewrite it as a − b > 0 to use in your proof. Formula: $a-b>0$
To prove LHS ≥ RHS, calculate their difference and show that LHS − RHS ≥ 0. Formula: $LHS - RHS \ge 0$
To prove an inequality for all real numbers, use completing the square to form $X^2$ or $X^2 + Y^2$.
For inequalities with ≥ or ≤, you must state the condition for equality.
For real numbers X, Y: $X^2 \ge 0$. Equality holds when $X = 0$.
To prove inequalities with radicals, calculate the difference of their squares, (LHS)^2 − (RHS)^2. Formula: $(LHS)^2-(RHS)^2$
When LHS > 0 and RHS > 0: (LHS)^2 > (RHS)^2 if and only if LHS > RHS. Formula: $(LHS)^2>(RHS)^2 \iff LHS>RHS$
(LHS)^2 ≥ (RHS)^2 if and only if LHS ≥ RHS (under the same condition LHS>0, RHS>0). Formula: $(LHS)^2\ge(RHS)^2 \iff LHS\ge RHS$
When a > 0, the square root of a is greater than 0. Formula: $a>0 \Rightarrow \sqrt{a}>0$
When a > 0, b > 0, (a+b)/2 ≥ √(ab), or a + b ≥ 2√(ab). Formula: $a>0, \ b>0, \ \frac{a+b}{2}\ge\sqrt{ab}$, or $a+b\ge 2\sqrt{ab}$
The AM-GM inequality is highly useful when the product of the terms simplifies to a constant. Example: a + 1/a ⇒ a × 1/a = 1. Formula: $a+\frac{1}{a}\Rightarrow a\times\frac{1}{a}=1$
